subject: Bluepine DPA: implementation checklist & redline coordination
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Li <emma.li@bluepine-labs.com>, procurement@bluepine-labs.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Bluepine DPA — initial redline and proposed next steps

Hi team,

Attaching the latest redline (Bluepine-DPA-redline-v3.docx) from procurement. They flagged two SCC-related asks (controller/processor mapping and cross-border routing) and want an implementation plan before Legal greenlights execution. High level:

- Bluepine needs confirmation we can restrict routing to EU regions for EU-subject data and provide a subprocessor inventory for any transfers.
- Procurement asked for a 30-day evidence window for audit logs tied to the order form.

Laura/Karthik — can Legal/Privacy confirm whether the proposed processor-delegation language in §3.2 is acceptable or if we should propose the standard delegation schedule? Also: is 30 days for log evidence reasonable from an ops perspective?

I propose a quick sync tomorrow to decide an approach (approve redline, propose counter, or offer implementation addendum). Emma — thanks for patience; we'll come back with a narrow execution plan that won't block your go-live.

Next steps I suggest: 1) legal quick review (Laura/Karthik) 2) ops check on retention routing (Grace) 3) proposed schedule to procurement (Ben) by EOD Thu.

Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Bluepine-DPA-redline-v3.docx (docx, 42KB); SCCs-mapping-20261124.xlsx (xlsx, 18KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Emma Li <emma.li@bluepine-labs.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Bluepine DPA — initial redline and proposed next steps

Thanks Ben — quick thoughts after initial read:

- The redline introduces a non-standard "routing carveout" that purports to lock data to EU regions. Our standard position is to offer contractual routing controls plus operational attestations, but not absolute geo-locking unless on Dedicated/Private. We should clarify whether Bluepine needs an enforceable geo-lock in the MSA/order form (i.e., a binding routing SLI) or whether an implementation addendum with region constraints and fallback is sufficient.
- The controller/processor mapping in §3.2 is okay provided subprocessor notice windows are aligned with their procurement ask. We should tighten the notification timing (from 30 to 14 days) if we can.
- 30-day audit log window: ops can generally provide 30 days of structured logs; longer retention is an add-on.

Proposed reply to Bluepine: propose an implementation addendum that documents routing defaults (EU primary), fallback behavior, and a 14-day subprocessor notice for material changes. If Bluepine insists on an absolute EU-only clause, we escalate to product for feasibility (likely Dedicated offering or Private deployment).

I can draft a concise email and a tracked-counter. If we want, loop in Product (Grace) for a single line on feasibility and costs.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Laura — appreciate the quick take. Operational constraints and notes:

- We can commit to EU-primary routing for customer traffic by default (Core-hosted) and document this in an implementation addendum. Full enforcement (preventing any token to non-EU infra) is only guaranteed on Dedicated/Private.
- We can export an ordered subprocessor roster and provide 30-day structured audit logs; if Bluepine requires 90 days, we can provide as an add-on with a cost delta.
- Implementation plan estimate: 3 business days to produce the addendum draft + IP for routing SLI; additional engineering work only if they request hard geo-locking.

Ben — if you can push the deadline to Fri EOD for our counter, we can include the addendum and a short product note about routing/upgrade paths.

Grace O'Connor
Head of Privacy Programs | Redwood Inference

From: Emma Li <emma.li@bluepine-labs.com>

Cc: procurement@bluepine-labs.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 Nov 2026 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Bluepine DPA — implementation checklist & redline coordination

Thanks — helpful notes. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Bluepine's primary requirement is that EU patient data NEVER transit outside EU jurisdictions during normal operation. We are open to an implementation addendum if it contains an explicit routing SLI and an operational escalation ladder.
2) Subprocessor notice: 14 days is acceptable.
3) Audit logs: 30 days is minimum; 90 days preferred but we can accept 30 for initial go-live with a plan to extend.

If Redwood can send the addendum and the tracked counter today, procurement will review and aim to return comments by Mon. If there's any language that requires Dedicated/Private to comply, call that out clearly so procurement can evaluate costs.

Emma Li
VP, Operations | Bluepine Labs
